issues.location: introductory link from inconsistency to model truth
issues.finding: The source says an inconsistent set cannot have all its formulas true at a world in any model, without specifying the system relative to which it is inconsistent. For a general modal system Sigma, soundness excludes such a world in a model of Sigma; an arbitrary model can still satisfy the set's formulas.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify both directions of the model-truth statement by the relevant system and models of that system.

issues.location: contrapositive proof of the consistency extension property
issues.finding: From the two extended sets being inconsistent, the proof says the two derivations of falsity follow by the preceding proposition's part b. They follow immediately from the definition of Sigma-consistency; part b instead characterizes derivability of a formula by inconsistency after adjoining its negation.
issues.proposed_resolution: Cite the definition of consistency in the target proof at this step while retaining the two displayed derivability claims.

translation_treatment: Translated consistency, examples and the contrapositive proof with system-relative model scope and the direct definition cited at the affected step.
